subject: Data Engineering
title: Lessons from Privacy Disasters
description: A quick, practical guide to Lessons from Privacy Disasters.

hook.text: Every privacy breach follows a pattern: access too broad, detection too slow, response too late.

buildup.text: Common causes: unpatched software, excessive permissions, unencrypted data, and poor monitoring.

discovery.text: Prevention requires defense in depth: encryption, least-privilege access, patching, and active monitoring.

twist.text: Breaches can't always be prevented. But detection in hours instead of years dramatically limits damage.

climax.text: The companies that survive breaches are those that detect fast, respond transparently, and fix root causes.

punchline.text: You can't prevent every breach. You can detect it fast.

quiz.question: What is the most critical factor in limiting breach damage?
